content.comment_body: Hello, I need guidance on practical steps to set up communication between a [company_name] [product_name] [article_no] and my laptop. I tried using an ethernet connection but could not establish communication. Thank you,

Hi [user_name], Welcome to the forum. Can you describe your issue in more detail? What exactly do you mean? Are you unable to connect [product_name] Access Tool to the [product_name], or is it something else?

Thanks for welcoming me. I'm experienced with GE and AB PLCs, but new to [company_name] PLCs. I am working with a stand-alone water filtration unit that uses a [company_name] [product_name] controller, which was installed before I joined this site. I need to clear some faults but can't connect to monitor the program online. I connected my laptop to the [product_name] using ethernet. Currently, my laptop runs [product_name] [product_name] software. Thank you,

Which [product_name] module do you have? Please provide the full order number. It starts with [article_no]. Which [product_name] software version are you using? What are the IP address and subnet mask of the [product_name]? What are the IP address and subnet mask of your laptop?
Thank you, I'm gathering this information now. Will share soon.
Order No.: [article_no] [product_name] Software Version: [version_no] [product_name] IP: 192.168.000.001 Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.000 Laptop PC: IP: 192.168.020.090 Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.000

Hi [user_name], You have two issues: 1) The [product_name] software version is not compatible with your [product_name]. You need [product_name] [version_no] or newer. If your current version is a full edition, you can upgrade for free to the latest [product_name] [version_no]. You can download the upgrade here: [document] The download is a 1.3 GB package. Once finished, run the setup as administrator. 2) The [product_name] and your PC are on different subnets. You need to change the subnet on one of the devices.
Thank you [user_name], 1) I'll download and upgrade the [product_name] software version now. 2) I thought the subnet masks were matching. Did you mean I should change the IP address?

Yes. An IP address has four segments. With a subnet mask of 255.255.255.0, the first three segments must be identical. XXX.XXX.XXX.YYY The first three sets (XXX.XXX.XXX) are the subnet, and the last set (YYY) is the device's address within the subnet.
Thank you for explaining so clearly. I appreciate your help.

analysis.insight_summary: The main user issue centers on connecting a laptop to a [company_name] [product_name] controller, with difficulties arising from software version incompatibility and incorrect network configuration. The user is unfamiliar with [company_name] products and struggles with interoperability, notably needing the right software version and matching subnet setup. The feedback highlights that newcomers to the system find both network setup and version requirements unclear, pointing to the need for improved onboarding guidance and documentation.
analysis.user_expectations: User anticipates a simple procedure to connect their laptop to the [product_name] controller via Ethernet, access the software program online, and resolve faults. They desire clear directions for achieving software compatibility and straightforward network configuration.
